correction.claim: Benham, writing in 1900, noted that the absence of minor lines on an otherwise well-formed hand should not be read as a deficiency.
correction.problem: docs/source-verification-log.md establishes twice, independently, that Benham does not read line absence at all: for the Mercury/health line, 'Benham does not read the line's absence at all; he reads the character of a line that is present,' and for the Sun Line, 'Benham says nothing of the kind.' No repository evidence supports Benham making this general reassurance.
correction.action: Attribution to Benham removed. Sentence restated as Palmistry Path's own editorial framing: 'This site does not read the absence of minor lines on an otherwise well-formed hand as a deficiency.' No replacement historical source was invented, and no vague anonymous authority ('modern palmists', 'some writers') was substituted for the removed attribution.
correction.surrounding_paragraph_check: The sentences immediately before and after the edited sentence make no source attribution and were left unchanged. The following paragraph ('Some hands carry a rich secondary layer... Others show only the major lines...') describes hand-to-hand variation directly rather than attributing a reading to any authority, and contains no prevalence/consensus wording; left unchanged.

source_preflight.notes: The Benham attribution was the sole scientific/historical claim in the focused passage; it was removed rather than reassigned to any other named source, per the task's explicit instruction not to invent a replacement historical meaning. No prevalence/consensus wording was introduced in the replacement sentence. No vague anonymous authority was introduced. No quotation marks were involved before or after this change. No combination reading was created — the replacement sentence makes no interpretive claim beyond the site's own editorial stance, already implicit in the surrounding paragraph's framing. Claim-type separation preserved: the replacement sentence is explicitly framed as this site's own position ('This site does not read...'), distinct from any historical or traditional claim. No medical, legal, financial, deterministic relationship, or predictive-science claim is present.
